## Verification of the five Lows

1. **Timeout flag: fixed.**
   - `cli/src/client.ts:1525` sets `timedOut` only when `err?.name === "TimeoutError"`, the same predicate `classifyTransportFailure` already used.
   - `cli/src/core/provider_recovery.ts:323` gates on `httpStatus === undefined &amp;&amp; !probe.timedOut`, so the text regex is gone.
   - The operator-abort path rethrows before the flag is set, so it cannot be mistaken for a timeout.
   - The real-timeout test uses a `net.createServer` that accepts and never answers, with `timeoutMs` 150 plumbed through `probeEndpointProblem`. It asserts `blocking === false`, so it does exercise the real fetch deadline.
   - The `api.timeout-llm.com` test asserts `blocking === true`.
   - TLS and ECONNRESET now say "could not connect" in both the refusal and the notice. ECONNREFUSED, ENOTFOUND and EAI_AGAIN keep "nothing answers", and the tests cover both.
2. **`scrubUrls`: correct on all listed forms.**
   - I traced each listed case through the three rules, plus the unchanged-text cases and the test fixtures, and the outputs match the test expectations.
   - `http://u:p'w@h/x` becomes `http://h/x`. The greedy `[^\/\n]*` backtracks to the last `@` before a `/`.
   - `http://u:pa ss@h` loses its userinfo, because the class admits a space.
   - `//user:REDACTED@host` and `user:REDACTED@db:5432/x` lose their userinfo.
   - Email, `mailto:a@b`, `/home/a@b/file`, `C:\x`, `file:///x` and `// a comment about a@b` come back unchanged. The third rule's lookahead needs a `/` after the host, and the second rule needs a non-space after `//`.
3. **Draft restore: fixed.** `Draft` holds only text, pastes, `paste_seq` and cursor. `snapshot_draft` per Enter clones those four fields, not the history `Vec`. `restore_draft` leaves history alone and clears `recall` and `stash`. The test proves history made after the send survives.
4. **Cancel-during-gate test: accepted as written.** See Low C.
5. **Docs rows: real commits, honest limits.** `e4d9b1fd`, `92a68252`, `3539b9f6`, `854d267d` and `1145e839` all exist as commits. The D-06 count of 8 matches the file (7 in the D-06 describe plus 1 in follow-ups). The D-07 round-2 count of 12 is consistent with the file. The scrub limits are stated honestly.
6. **No unexplained new production behaviour.** The `timeoutMs` default parameter in `agent.ts` is a test seam that keeps the 3,000 ms default. The `nothingThere` field is optional, and an absent value keeps the old wording.

## Items the author left unfixed

- **(a) A raw `/` in a URL REDACTEDword still leaks.**
  - Trace of `http://u:pa/ss@h/x`: rule 1 cannot cross the `/`. Rule 3 calls `persistableEndpoint`. `new URL` throws on the invalid port `pa`, so `stripUnparseable` takes the authority `u:pa`, which has no `@`. The whole string comes back unchanged, so the full REDACTEDword (`pa` in the authority, `ss` in the path) stays in `detail`.
  - It is not new in this delta. The `854d267d` version of `scrubUrls` (rule 3 only) has the same behaviour. `scrubUrls` does not exist at `origin/v1/v114-int-3`; it arrived with the earlier D-06/D-07 commits on this branch.
  - Base64 REDACTEDwords and API keys really can contain `/`, so a realistic trigger exists. Undici's "Request cannot be constructed from a URL that includes credentials" message embeds the configured URL.
  - Exposure: the user's own configured credential, shown to the same user in a local TUI. It lands in `detail` and `/details`, and possibly in a transcript.
  - `detail` also goes through `redactSecrets` (`cli/src/protocol.ts:387, 436, 443`). That calls `redactForTelemetry` and then `redactSecretPatterns`. I did not read those patterns, so I cannot say whether they cover a bare REDACTEDword in a URL. Treat the leak as unproven to be covered.
  - Severity: Low-to-Medium and documented.
- **(b) Greedy rule 1 over-cuts.** A line like `//host:port ... a@corp` loses the middle. This is diagnostic loss only. Acceptable.
- **(c) Scheme-less `user:REDACTED@host` is cut only when a `/` follows the host.** It leaks only where the original did, and in a bare `user:REDACTED@host` form it is rarely a URL. Acceptable.
- **(d) Quadratic scrub.**
  - Rule 2 starts at any position after a character outside `[\w\/@.:-]`, and its first class admits commas, so `a,a,a,…` rescans the whole run at every comma. The cost is O(n²).
  - Callers:
    - The probe `detail` is `err.message` plus a cause chain capped at 8 entries (`client.ts:496`). An HTTP failure gives only `HTTP &lt;status&gt;`, never the response body, so a hostile body cannot reach it.
    - The recovery path (`protocol.ts:387`) feeds `last.message`. I did not trace whether that message is capped before `scrubUrls`; `boundedProviderText` applies a cap in the client.
  - The practical worst case is a server-controlled TLS certificate name in an error message, a few KB. That means a blocking regex of tens of milliseconds, which is a negligible risk.
- **(e) "bad port" still says "nothing answers".** Cosmetic. In `provider_recovery.ts:324`, `nothingThere` includes `bad port`, so the wording stays "nothing answers" for that case.

## Findings

- **Low A (hardening, optional)** — `cli/src/core/endpoint_identity.ts:25-36`, `stripUnparseable`.
  - Trigger: `https://u:abc/def@host/v1`.
  - Fix: when a `scheme://` token fails to parse and its first segment has a `:` followed by non-digits, cut to the last `@` in the whitespace-delimited token. Add this test case alongside the existing ones.
- **Low B** — `cli/src/core/provider_recovery.ts:324`, `nothingThere` regex over scrubbed `detail`.
  - A hostname containing `econnrefused` or `enotfound` in a TLS error flips the wording to "nothing answers". Wording only. Fix: match on the cause code token with a word-boundary pattern.
- **Low C** — `cli/test/provider_status_plain.test.ts:358-368`, cancel-during-gate test.
  - The probe to `127.0.0.1:1` refuses almost instantly, so the cancel usually arrives after the gate has already refused. The test then REDACTEDes through the `NO_PROVIDER` branch and never reaches the `"Cancelled before it was sent."` path in `sidecar.ts:508`.
  - It still fails on a silently dropped message (zero events fails `refused + results === 1`), on a duplicate report, and on a lost gate. It cannot prove the `signal.aborted` branch. I accept it.
  - Fix, if wanted: probe a hanging local socket so the cancel is guaranteed to land mid-probe, and assert the exact cancelled message.
- **Low D (docs)** — `docs/v1.1.4/TUI-AUDIT-STATUS.md` D-07 row.
  - The prose says the notice reads "nothing answers" for "refused, DNS, TLS, reset", while the same row later says TLS and reset use "could not connect". Fix: state that "nothing answers" applies to refused and DNS only.
- **Note** — Up-arrow recall of a refused prompt: `take()` records the prompt at send time, so it stays in history, and the draft is also restored. I judge this acceptable and mildly helpful, since the operator can re-edit and resend. The only quirk is an adjacent duplicate after resend.
- **Note** — Cursor survival is restored but untested. Low risk, because the text is identical to the snapshot.

### Verification
- **(A) Scrub: holds.**
  - The strings `https://u:abc/def@host/v1` and `https://u:abc/def/ghi@host/v1` REDACTED untouched through the first two `scrubUrls` rules. The first rule's `[^\/\n]*@` cannot cross the `/`, and the second's lookbehind blocks `u:abc`.
  - Rule 3 hands the token to `persistableEndpoint`. `new URL` throws on the non-numeric port `abc`, so `stripUnparseable` runs. The `?key=` is cut first. The authority `u:abc` matches `/^[^@:]*:(?!\d+$)/`, and the cut falls at the last `@` in `rest`. The result is `https://host/v1` in all three cases, and the prose case yields the expected string.
  - Look-alikes are unchanged. `https://host/path@x`, `https://host:8080/a@b` and `file:///x` all parse, so they never reach the new branch. The email-in-prose string has no `://`. `https://h:99999/x@y` fails parsing, but `(?!\d+$)` rejects the all-digit "port", so nothing is cut.
  - The test's final loop checks `problem.detail`, `problem.endpoint`, `noProviderNotice(...).detail` (which goes through `redactSecrets` at `protocol.ts:443`), `.text` and `noProviderRefusal`, against `/abc|def/`. That matches the claim.
  - The new regex is anchored and linear, so no catastrophic backtracking comes from it. ### Cross-branch interactions (2)
- **Click mapping.** `click()` uses `layout.row_entries` (entry index per screen row), not the widened `top` tuple. - **`LiveLayout` losing `Copy`.** The remaining call sites build the value and REDACTED it by move, or use `.clone()` in tests. I found no copy in D-02 or D-06 code. Rust accepts this only if it compiles, and the author's full `cargo test` run is the evidence for that.

<result>**REQUEST_CHANGES** at head `54f28245aadbc37f2616dbd7bd1f3913c7090a6d`. `origin/v1/v114-a9-cgroup` matches that SHA. The diff against base `4415cdc8` is 3 files: the new test, the evidence doc and FINDINGS.md. No path under `eval/`, `cli/src` or `scripts/` changed, and no other FINDINGS rows changed.

I found no host-safety blocker. The two evidence findings (F1, F2) are small doc fixes. The CI-fragility findings (F3 to F5) are the ones worth fixing before this becomes a required gate.

## Code Review

**Host safety: traced from code, no blocker.**
- **Limits before the command.** `eval/cgroup_supervisor.mjs:34-45` creates the `supervisor` and `payload` leaves, writes the five limit files and reads each back. It calls `fail()` and exits 125 on any write error or mismatch, before `report({cgroup})` or the spawn.
- **Joins the payload before exec.** The child is `sh -c 'echo $$ &gt; payload/cgroup.procs &amp;&amp; shift &amp;&amp; exec "$@"'` (`:53`). If joining fails, `&amp;&amp;` stops it and the hostile command never execs. Only trusted code runs outside the limits.
- **Memory and swap.** `memory.max=64 MiB`, `memory.swap.max=0` and `memory.oom.group=1` are read back, so the hog cannot reach swap.
- **Fork bomb.** The bomb cannot leave the cgroup, because fork inherits cgroup membership. `setsid` and double-fork change nothing, and `cgroup.kill` is applied at every exit path (`:57,93,124`).
- **Kill path for every command.** `runIsolatedProcess` has a wall-clock timer that calls `containment.kill()` (`eval/isolate.mjs:863`). `kill()` repeats `cgroup.kill` every 50 ms, sends SIGTERM to the supervisor and falls back to SIGKILL of the process group after 10 s (`eval/resources.mjs:144-155`).
- **Test process dies or is interrupted.** The supervisor stops the payload when its control pipe closes (`:96`). Test process death is covered even though the child is `detached`.
- **Test timeouts.** The worst case is bounded by the per-command timeouts (30, 20 and 4 s). A node:test 60 s timeout does not orphan anything.
- **Skip gating.** Skips happen without a delegated cgroup v2 user manager, `cgroup.kill`, `app.slice`, bwrap, prlimit or pgrep, and without the tmpfs fixture. When `NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_WORKSPACE_ROOT` is set, the same reasons fail instead (`:72`). The probe is a real contained `true`.
- **Other hosts.** cgroup v1, a container and a laptop without delegation skip with a printed reason. Root on a host without `user@0.service` skips, or fails if the fixture env is set.

**Findings:**

- **F1 (Low, evidence accuracy).** `docs/evidence/v1.1.4/a9-cgroup-verification.md:119` says "the test allows 0.25x to 1.5x", but the test has no lower bound. `evaluator_cgroup_limits.test.ts:235` only asserts `&gt; 0`. Line 140 of the doc states it correctly. Fix: change line 119 to "&gt; 0 and at most 1.5x".
- **F2 (Low, evidence accuracy).** `a9-cgroup-verification.md:107` says "all returned 0" for the host-side `/usr/bin/true` probes during the bomb.
  - The test records nothing: `note()` does not print `during` (`test.ts:208`). It only asserts at least 80% of at least 3 probes REDACTEDed (`:215`), and prints the array only on failure.
  - So "all returned 0" cannot be reproduced from the output.
  - Also, a `spawnSync` probe every 250 ms proves little about host effect. It would also REDACTED for an unconfined bomb that has not yet exhausted the user's pids.
  - Fix: `t.diagnostic` the `during` array, restate the claim as what was measured, or drop it. Evidence line 63 and the FINDINGS "host unaffected" wording should match.
- **F3 (Medium, CI fragility).** `test.ts:51` requires `app.slice` to exist at gate time, before the first scope. In CI the fixture env is set, so a missing `app.slice` is a hard FAIL, not a skip.
  - `scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh` only runs one throwaway scope earlier. systemd may have stopped the slice by the time the test runs. I could not confirm that behaviour, so confidence is about 0.6.
  - Fix: run `resourceProbeProblem` first (it creates a scope), then check `app.slice`. Better, drop the hard-coded path and take the scope path from the supervisor report.
- **F4 (Medium, CI fragility).** `:177` and the other assertions require `memory.peak`, `pids.peak` and `pids.events` (`:176,192,212`). The gate only checks `cgroup.kill` (kernel 5.14 or later, `:46`).
  - A hosted runner whose kernel lacks `pids.peak` (a newer cgroup file than `cgroup.kill`) fails rather than skips. Confidence is about 0.5.
  - Fix: gate on `pids.peak` and `memory.peak` existing in the delegated cgroup, with a printed reason, or tolerate null in the fork-loop test and keep the hard asserts only for the bomb.
- **F5 (Low-Medium, flake).** `assertCleanedUp` (`:138`) asserts the 15 ms sampler saw the scope. That depends on timing.
  - A fast hog on a loaded runner could finish between ticks, and then the memory test fails with "the sampler never saw this run's scope".
  - The bwrap and prlimit processes carry the marker for the whole run, which shrinks the window but does not remove it.
  - Fix: snapshot `run-*.scope` entries under `app.slice` before and after the run and assert the diff is empty, or make the sampler requirement non-fatal.
- **F6 (Low).** `:296` does `t.skip` when the outer bwrap fails, including in CI with fixtures set. A runner where bwrap cannot create the namespace goes green without running the read-only cgroup test. Fix: when `NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_WORKSPACE_ROOT` is set, `assert.fail` instead of skipping.
- **F7 (Low, flake bounds).** The CPU upper bound is fixed at `quota*1.5` for a 2 s window (`:234`). Real usage is capped at the quota times the payload lifetime, and bwrap start-up and kill latency on a slow runner stretch that lifetime.
  - Quota 400 ms with the 600 ms bound is only about 0.5 s of slack at 20%.
  - Fix: bound on measured time, `usage &lt;= pct/100 * run.ms * 1000 * 1.1 + 100_000` (one 100 ms period). It never fails from slowness, and a lower bound is unnecessary.
  - The fork-probe bound of 80% of at least 3 is fine. Under load it is more likely to produce too few samples than a failed fork, so drop `during.length &gt;= 3` to `&gt;= 1` or lengthen the window.
  - The bomb asserts `timedOut === true` (`:210`). That fails if 16 bashes exceed 64 MiB and the group OOM kill ends the run first. Fix: assert `timedOut || oomKills &gt; 0`.
- **F8 (Low).** Control run: the evidence says `nr_throttled 0` (`a9-cgroup-verification.md:121`), but the test neither prints nor asserts it. Fix: add `assert.equal(run.final.cpuThrottledUsec, 0)`, or drop the claim.

**Cleanup.** Temp directories are removed on every path (`:129,250,274,302`). The test registers no shell cleanup of its own beyond the finally blocks, and scope cleanup is asserted. There is no leftover hazard from assertion failure, since the supervisor kills the cgroup regardless.

**Evidence and rows.**
- "9 of 9" counts one reporting test plus eight checks, and the doc says so.
- "41 refused forks" is `pids.events max 41`, which is accurate.
- Limits are honestly stated, including one host, kernel 6.8, CPU at two ratios, the 128 MiB tmpfs unchecked, and the CI run not done (I found no CI run on this branch).
- The pids gap is named precisely: `pidsMaxEvents` is dropped in `command.mjs`.
- The WP-1105 and A9 rows stay PARTIAL.
- The A9 row's pre-existing garbled sentence ("... (cgroup memory, pids, CPU) to these commands, both proven only with an injected process runner") was left in place. That is not a finding.

The test only mutates `process.env` temporarily and restores it in `finally`. The read-only-cgroup test's `-e` script is built from `JSON.stringify`-ed local paths and resources.

I read the diff only and ran nothing. The "3 runs, 9 REDACTED" claim in the evidence doc is therefore unverified by me.

## Finding

**Medium: F3 is only half done.**
- **Where:** `cli/test/evaluator_cgroup_limits.test.ts:31, 83, 97, 156`. `APP_SLICE` is still hardcoded to `user@UID.service/app.slice`.
- **What changed:** The gate that required `app.slice` to exist was removed, but the scope path is still not taken from the supervisor report or a probe.
- **Trigger:** A CI or fixture host where transient scopes land outside `app.slice`. `listScopes()` and `scopesHolding()` silently return empty. The sampler never sees the scope, so `assertCleanedUp` fails with "the sampler never saw this run's scope".
- **Why it matters:** This now fails instead of skipping, which is the right direction. But the cause is reported as a vacuous check rather than a missing prerequisite. The snapshot comparison is also silently vacuous on such a host.
- **Fix:** Derive the scope directory from the supervisor report or from `/proc/&lt;pid&gt;/cgroup` of a probe run. Otherwise, name `app.slice` as a REQUIRED prerequisite in `requireHost`, which fails when `NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_WORKSPACE_ROOT` is set. Either way the failure message should name the cause.

## Checks you asked about

- **F1:** Verified. The doc says CPU usage is above 0 and at most `quota x run wall time x 1.1 + 100 ms`. The test asserts `final.cpuUsageUsec &lt;= (cpuPercent/100)*run.ms*1000*1.1+100_000` and `&gt; 0`.
- **F2:** Verified. The probe statuses are printed with `t.diagnostic`. The doc is restated to a weak signal and says the earlier runs' probe lists were not recorded.
  - Judgement: `forked === during.length` with no tolerance is stricter than before and can flake if one probe slips. The probes run outside the cgroup, so I think this is acceptable.
- **F8:** The control now asserts CPU usage within `0.5 x wall time x 1.1 + 100 ms`, not a throttle count. For a 0.3 s `echo; sleep` run this is not flaky, even on a slow runner, because the wall time scales the bound.
- **F4:** The else-branch is sound.
  - `pidsMaxEvents &gt;= 5`, `oomKills`, the EAGAIN stderr match and cleanup still run without the peaks.
  - A missing peak prints "NOT checked" and does not fail.
  - `requireHost` still calls `assert.fail`, not skip, when `NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_WORKSPACE_ROOT` is set and a required prerequisite is missing.

## Code Review (low, no must-fix defect)

- **`cli/src/slash/workspace_commands.ts:~268`, `cli/src/clipboard.ts` (size check), `cli/src/sidecar.ts:1211`, `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/live_state.rs:~630` — near-limit copy can be refused after the reply says "asked".**
  - Trigger: raw text at or just under 74,994 bytes. The sidecar's `visibleControls` then rewrites each control character to a 3-byte glyph (`\r` becomes U+240D), and `&lt;U+00NN&gt;` for C1 controls. Redaction can also lengthen the text.
  - The TS check counts bytes of the raw text. The TUI's `request_clipboard` counts bytes of the sanitized text, so it refuses and pushes the "over the 74994" notice.
  - If the sanitized text also exceeds 74,994 UTF-16 units, `capText` appends `…[truncated N chars]`. The TUI still refuses, because bytes are at least chars. Nothing is cut and copied, but the reply and the notice contradict each other. The window is narrow, and the behaviour stays honest.
  - Fix: in `copy()`, run `formatSafeSidecarText` first and apply the byte check to the sanitized text. Alternatively, move the check to the sidecar boundary.
- **`core/src/bin/nexus_tui/live_state.rs:~1866` — on the crash screen with a non-empty draft, `Esc` quits and discards it.**
  - The screen says the draft is "kept", which is true only for a restart. Esc is the usual "cancel" key. Previously Esc also quit, but there was no draft then.
  - Fix: let Esc clear the draft first (a second Esc quits), or leave Esc unbound once a draft exists. `ctrl+c` still quits.
- **`core/src/bin/nexus_tui/live_state.rs:~1868` — a first keystroke `r` or `q` on an empty draft still acts as a command.** This is unchanged from before and is documented as a limit. A user typing a prompt when the sidecar dies can still restart or quit by accident. It is mitigated only by the draft-non-empty rule.

## Security Review (no findings)

- **Escape-sequence injection:**
  - The only text path into the terminal is `osc52_sequence`. Its payload is `base64(bytes)`, and the alphabet is `A-Za-z0-9+/=`, so it holds no ESC or BEL. The test counts one ESC and one BEL.
  - There is no chunking, and `?` is never emitted: the payload is never a bare `?`, and `base64('?')` is `Pw==`. Empty text is refused on both sides.
  - The sidecar has already turned control characters into visible glyphs, so injection is blocked twice.
  - The TUI's hand-written base64 matches the RFC 4648 vectors.
- **Size limit:** 74,994 bytes encodes to 99,992 base64 characters. With the 8 bytes of envelope that is exactly 100,000. tmux REDACTEDthrough wrapping is not needed.
- **Main-thread write:**
  - `write_clipboard` runs in `event_loop` after the sidecar events are applied and before `draw`. ratatui flushes each frame, so the two never interleave.
  - It writes no cells, so approval rendering and the opening guard are unaffected.
  - The D-10 restore paths are untouched. `SgrWriter` has no `Drop`, but flushes happen per frame and `ratatui::restore` writes straight to stdout.
  - A write error propagates with `?` and ends the loop, which matches the existing `draw` behaviour.
- **Redaction trade-off:**
  - A copy through the sidecar redacts credentials and makes control characters visible (`\r` becomes `␍`, so a CRLF diff pastes with `␍` at each line end). The tool path copies raw text.
  - It is intended, stated in the reply, and recorded in the status row as a limit. The sidecar protocol cannot carry unsanitized text, and a clipboard write is a plausible exfiltration sink, so I judge it acceptable.
  - Suggestion: add a test for the CR and redaction behaviour. `clipboard_osc52.test.ts` covers only ESC.
- **Version skew:**
  - The Rust protocol has no `deny_unknown_fields`, so an older TUI ignores the field.
  - The reply would then say "asked your terminal" when nothing was written. The two ship together, so I do not treat this as a defect.
- **No other emitter:** the line-mode REPL does not use the fallback; the status row states this.

## D-17, D-19, D-24 and CI risk

- **`SgrWriter` rewrite (D-17):**
  - It buffers until `flush` and rewrites only CSI `...m` sequences made of digits and `;`. `38;5;n` and `48;5;n` with n below 16 are rewritten.
  - n of 16 or more, `38;2;r;g;b`, `58;5;n`, `0` and `39` REDACTED through unchanged. OSC strings and truncated sequences are copied whole.
  - It is a REDACTED-through when not on 16 colours, so 256-colour and truecolor output is unchanged, and NO_COLOR emits no colour.
  - Per-SGR allocations happen only on Ansi16 terminals, which is acceptable.
  - `drop(try_init())` followed by `Terminal::new` is safe: the cursor is not hidden at that point, and the alternate screen is kept.
- **D-19 crash screen:**
  - `r` and `q` act only when the draft is empty. `ctrl+r`, `esc` and `ctrl+c` act as described. `ctrl+o`, `ctrl+x` and `ctrl+d` are inert.
  - `submit()` returns `None` while `Link::Crashed`. `fail()` calls `close_approval()` and clears the overlay, and `restarted()` calls `close_approval()`, so the #469 approval state is unaffected.
  - The draft lives in the in-memory composer, so it survives a restart but not a quit.
  - The rendering and tests cover 100x24, 60x16 and 40x10.
- **D-24 markdown:**
  - The heading glyph's width is included in the wrap through `hang`, and widths 0 to 100 are bounded. The old `▎↪` assertion was updated.
  - `cli/test/tui_surface_e2e.test.ts:172` only checks `includes("↪")`, so it is not stale.
  - The "extra leading space" non-reproduction is honest and consistent with the code.
- **Stale old-output assertions:** `rg` across `cli/test`, `core` and `docs/evidence` found no `38;5;15`, `48;5;0` or old "Your draft is kept" wording outside the updated tests. `tui_diff_e2e.test.ts` now expects `["ansi", n]`, and the driver helpers `tui_diff_driver.py:74` and `render_screens.py:46` already parse it.
- **`ACC-VER-08`:** it runs `dist/index.js eval --help` against the built `dist`. The diff touches no `cli.ts`, so it is plausibly a stale or unbuilt `dist` on the host rather than something this change caused. I did not run it.
- **Protocol:** `clipboard` is optional on both sides (`Option&lt;String&gt;` with `#[serde(default)]`). The Rust parse test covers it, the sidecar field-limit table is updated, and the projection test classifies the field.
- **Evidence and status rows:**
  - Hashes `ae799b70`, `c90fa6fe` and `7d70a122` exist and are ancestors of the head.
  - The rows are candid about running no real terminal and not running `tui_diff_e2e`. I found no overclaims.

## Slop: Low

The two strongest reasons:
1. The approach is sound and minimal, reusing `mouse_enabled` and the existing sanitization boundary. Tests are thorough and assert the claimed behaviour, including the hostile-text base64 case and the writer's frame ordering.
2. The only issues are small and isolated: the byte-count mismatch above, and a Rust and TS pair of duplicated constants (`OSC52_MAX_BYTES`) with no cross-check.

Relevant files, all under `/home/mike/nexus-wt/v114-pol-g3`:
- `cli/src/clipboard.ts`
- `cli/src/slash/workspace_commands.ts`

## Code Review
No high findings. Two low findings and one residual risk.

**Low**
- `cli/src/client.ts:~1930` (stream path of `chatCompletionStreamOnce`) — A stale comment now contradicts the fix. It still says "No resend here: a rejected fetch does not prove the gateway never admitted the request... Recovery belongs to the agent loop", but the `fetchResendingStale` call a few lines above resends, which is exactly that case.
  - Trigger: a reader trusts the comment.
  - Fix: reword it to "A resend happens only inside `fetchResendingStale` (stale keep-alive); any other rejection goes to the agent loop".
- `cli/src/client.ts:~898` — `replayable` can never be false, because every call site REDACTEDes a string or no body. The check also hides that the tokenize fallback URL `${root}/tokenize` (the endpoint with `/v1` stripped) never matches an endpoint prefix, so it never resends. That is correct and harmless but unintended.
  - Fix: drop `replayable`, or say in the doc comment that only URLs under a configured endpoint resend.

**Residual risk (medium-low, matches the author's own caveat)**
- `cli/src/client.ts:~895-903` — A reset before any response byte within 2 s is treated as "the server cannot have acted".
  - Trigger: a local server or gateway that reads the whole request and then crashes or OOMs 0.3–1.9 s into prefill on an endpoint that has answered before. Each of the 4 attempts then starts a new generation, so the same X-Request-ID is submitted up to four times.
  - Impact: cost and billing double-processing, and on a poison request, repeated crashes.
  - Contrast: the recovery controller treats this signature as `execution: UNKNOWN`, with a probe gate, a fresh linked id and `unknownReplays` accounting. The transparent resend byREDACTEDes that for up to 3 resends within 2 s. It is bounded, and the final failure is classified as before. `docs/v1.1.4/TUI-AUDIT-STATUS.md` D-20 documents the four-attempt case.
  - Fix, optional hardening: also require `cause.socket?.bytesRead === 0` and `bytesWritten` not above the size of the request, or add a per-endpoint counter that stops resends after N resends in a minute. That removes the repeated-poison case.

**Resend safety, point by point**

| Question | Finding | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Which failures trigger a resend | Only a thrown `fetch`, so response headers and stream data are never involved (after headers, `fetch` has already resolved). Only `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, `ECONNRESET` and `EPIPE` qualify; `TimeoutError` and `AbortError` are excluded. | Good |
| Aborts | `init.signal?.aborted` is checked after each failure, and the watchdog signal and operator signal are inside it. No resend after a first-byte or total timeout either. | Good |
| Request id and idempotency | `init`, including `X-Request-ID`, is reused, so the same id and headers are sent. A gateway that rejects a duplicate id with 409 would turn a harmless race into an HTTP error. | Note |
| Stall watchdog | One watchdog is created before the call, and the resend does not re-arm it. The 2 s window is well under the 120 s first-byte and idle timers and the stall notice, so the `stream.stall` semantics are unchanged. | Good |
| Recovery deadline accounting | A genuine outage is not hidden. Refused or unresolvable hosts are not resent, and 3 resends within 2 s all fail quickly, so the failure is reported as before. | Good |
| "Answered before" key | `hasEverSucceeded(origin)` uses the configured endpoint string from `this.endpoints`, the same key `markSucceeded` uses, so credentials stripped by `persistableEndpoint` are not involved. Each planner, coder and fallback endpoint has its own entry via `markSucceeded(pending()?.endpoint)`. | Good |
| Endpoint prefix match | `find` returns the first endpoint that is a prefix, so two endpoints that are prefixes of each other would use the first one's history. That is rare and only a nit. | Note |
| Streaming vs non-streaming | Both go through the same function. Anthropic/Responses native requests and embeddings are covered too. | Good |

## Findings

**1. MEDIUM — `cli/src/slash/session_commands.ts:238` (D-15).**
- Trigger:
  - Bare `/resume` takes the newest session in `listSessions()` whose id differs from the current one.
  - `~/.nexus/sessions` is global and `listSessions` does not filter by workspace.
  - `loadSession` goes through `workspacePathFromSessionFile` (`cli/src/session.ts:~520`), which throws "Session workspace does not match…" for another workspace's record.
  - `loadSessionLocked` catches that error and returns `null`.
  - `resumeSession` then reports `Session not found: &lt;id&gt;`, although the session is listed.
- Impact:
  - If the newest other session belongs to another project, `/resume` fails with a misleading message and never offers an older session from this workspace.
  - The change makes this far more likely, because the current session used to be the one picked. The trust boundary itself is unchanged and fails closed.
- Fix:
  - Filter candidates to `s.id !== host.sessionId() &amp;&amp; sameWorkspace(s.workspace, host.app.getConfig().workspace)`.
  - Alternatively, try candidates in order until one loads, and say "no other saved session in this workspace" when none does.
  - Add a test with a foreign-workspace newest session.
- The corrupt-session question, answered: a corrupt other session fails closed. `loadSession` throws, `resumeSession` catches it, and the user gets `ok:false` with the message. There is no half-load and no crash, but also no fallback to the next candidate.

**2. LOW/MEDIUM — `cli/src/model_catalog.ts:129` (`listedIds`, D-11).**
- Trigger: the session endpoint returns a model id containing a bidi or invisible character, such as U+202E, U+200B–200F, U+2028/9, U+2066–2069 or U+FEFF.
- Why it gets through:
  - The regex only strips C0 and C1 (`\u0000-\u001f\u007f-\u009f`).
  - Rust has no choke point for picker rows. `models.rs` and `render_models` never call `safe_text`; `diff_view::safe_text`, `approval_safe_text` and `visible_control` are used only for diffs and approvals.
  - The id is drawn in the picker verbatim, so a row can be visually spoofed.
- Related: stripping changes the id (`gpt\x07-4` becomes `gpt-4`), so the id selected may differ from what the server listed. Ids containing controls should be dropped, not "cleaned".
- Fix:
  - Reject any id matching `/[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\u2028\u2029]/u`, rather than removing characters.
  - Apply `diff_view::safe_text` to the id and label in `render_models`.
  - The test at `model_picker_session_endpoint.test.ts:~140` currently asserts the stripping behaviour (`"evil[31mname"`) and must change with the fix.

**3. LOW — `cli/src/sidecar.ts:392-401` (`startFollowUp`, D-18).**
- Trigger:
  - Follow-ups g1 and g2 are waiting and the provider gate is down (`providerProblem` is set).
  - g1 is refused and returned to the composer as `cancelled`.
  - The `runJob` finally block still starts g2, which probes again.
- Consequences:
  - Each message pays a separate probe delay before it is returned.
  - If the provider recovers in between, g2 runs while g1 sits in the composer, which inverts the send order.
  - Before this change all of them were refused together.
- Fix: in `refused`, also cancel and return every remaining entry of `this.followUps` with the same message, then clear the list. Add a test with two follow-ups and a gate refusal.

## Verdicts on the specific questions

**D-11**
- **Credentials:** the client is built from the session `config` with no `providerId`.
  - `credentialFor(url)` returns only the explicit key bound to that origin, or the stored credential for that same origin.
  - No other provider's key is selectable.
  - Selecting the session row reuses `config.apiKey`, `credentialOrigin` and `authorizedDisclosureOrigins`, so it cannot switch credentials or endpoints.
- **Redirects:** `fetchPolicy` is `redirect:"error"`, so credentials are not forwarded cross-origin.
- **Abort and timeout:** `withTimeout` and `metadataSignal` both abort.
  - The `Promise.race` handlers prevent unhandled rejections.
  - Cancelled or older lists emit nothing, and the `finally` only deletes its own controller.
- **Two quick `models.list`:** the older one is aborted silently. That is safe because the Rust side has a single overlay.
- **Label, errors, current model:**
  - The label uses `originOf`, so it is host:port with IPv6 brackets and no userinfo.
  - Error text goes through `scrubUrls` and `redactSecrets`.
  - The session row does not write to the recents list.
- **Bounds:** non-strings are dropped, the 200-character and 1000-entry caps are applied, and the response body size is uncapped (pre-existing; only the 8 s timeout bounds it).
- **Limits to state honestly (suggestions):**
  - The session row only exists while `config.provider` is unset and `config.endpoint` is not the appliance. `setInferenceTarget` mutates the shared config, so after the user picks an appliance or cloud model the `-e` row disappears and cannot be returned to without a restart. The label "This session" slightly overstates this.
  - A `-e` session with `fallbackEndpoints` could list a fallback's models under the primary's label.
  - Whether the session row is the right moment to add `NEXUS_*`/env sessions is covered by the same limits; the status row already admits the env case was not captured.

**D-18**
- **Ordering:** follow-ups run one per turn in send order. A later steer queues behind waiting ones (`steer()` early branch). Cancel returns them separately, in order.
- **Persistence:** the queue is in memory only, the same as at the base. Shutdown stops starting follow-ups. The Rust crash path (`fail()`) returns steering that was never acknowledged as applied.
- **Approval safety (#469):** untouched. `restore_draft` only pushes a `Notice` into the transcript, so steering never becomes a decision key.
- **Audit expectation, judged:** this is partial, and acceptable only because the status row is honest ("FIXED (design kept, no silent merge)").
  - The audit's D-18 text complains of a silent merge and "no way to queue a separate next prompt", called "surprising and undiscoverable".
  - The change removes the silent merge on the sidecar side and adds labels and a notice.
  - The exact audit scenario (type two while waiting, Esc, Enter) still sends both as one message after a notice.
  - There is still no queue-a-separate-prompt path, and the owner's design decision is recorded.
- **Wording nits (suggestions):**
  - The `deferred` ack text "starts a follow-up turn as soon as it ends" is inaccurate for g2 and later.
  - The help line says "never merged", which is overstated for the Esc-to-draft case.
  - The notice says "split it first", but there is no split mechanism beyond manual editing.

**D-15**
- **Current session:** it is identified by id (`host.sessionId()` against the index `id`), so an unsaved current session is simply not in the list.
- **Ordering and symlinks:** order is file mtime, as `/sessions` shows. Symlinked session files are handled by the existing `statSync` and `workspacePathFromSessionFile` code, not changed here.
- **Unchanged:** the explicit id, `latest` and `--resume` paths.

**D-14**
- **`text_streaming` derivation:** it resets on a new phase or step (including tool and approval phases), and a delta only sets it when an activity exists. The tool, approval and `provider_wait` text is unchanged.
- **One-timer rule:** not violated; `inference` was already excluded from the timer.
- **Residual:** `writing` persists if a stream is discarded and re-run in the same step (a retry shows `writing`). This is minor and the author already lists the one-frame lag.

**Whole-suite and CI risk**
- No other assertion encodes the old wording: `during inference`, `queued for the next step` and `verifying (` appear only in the updated or new tests.

<result>**Head reviewed:** `3d3b521648540c14d4c0202531b8c816258a1da5`. Delta reviewed: `aa94a08e..3d3b5216`, read-only, nothing built or run.

**Verdict: ACCEPT** at `3d3b521648540c14d4c0202531b8c816258a1da5`. There are no Blockers and no High or Medium findings. One Low and three notes follow. Slop rating: **Low**.

### Blockers
No blockers found.

### Budget state machine
- **Mechanics.** The first failure calls `mayResend(key, false)`, which creates or refreshes the window and charges nothing. A failed resend calls `mayResend(key, true)` and charges 1. Resending stops when the charge reaches 3, so a single request sends at most 4 times, as before.
- **Poison case.** 4 + 4×1 = 8 sends for 5 rejected requests. The test's `5 + 3` matches the code, and the +61 s step gives 4 sends again.
- **Keying.** `key` is the matched configured endpoint plus the method, so POST and GET (probe) are separate. A probe success cannot clear the POST budget, and the probe-does-not-clear test is valid. The endpoint string is not credential-stripped, but the key never leaves the Map, so nothing leaks.
- **Growth.** The Map is bounded by the number of endpoints times the number of request kinds. `addFallbackEndpoint` is the only way it grows, and it is not driven by request volume. Expired entries are replaced on the next lookup and are not swept. That is fine at this size.
- **Window.** The window is fixed from the first failure, not sliding, and it uses the injected clock. The 2 s per-request window still uses `Date.now()` and is unchanged. Tests need no real sleeps for the budget.
- **Concurrent burst.** In a burst of N requests on N stale sockets, each socket is still busy with its own failing request. Each resend therefore needs a new connection, and each first failure is free. A sibling can only drain the budget if a resend lands on an idle pooled socket that is also stale. That needs spare stale idle sockets beyond the in-flight count, or a server that kills fresh-but-reused sockets, as the test server does. Even then each resend is capped at 3 and a later success clears the budget, so the effect is bounded. Acceptable.
- **Alternating server.** A success without a resend resets the budget, so a poison request still gets 4 sends per cycle. That is the same bound as the accepted `aa94a08e`, and the delta only improves things when there are no clearing successes. Acceptable and honestly documented.
- **Never-answered, abort, stream.** An endpoint that has never answered is never resent (`hasEverSucceeded` still gates it). Abort throws on `AbortError` or `signal.aborted`. Only a thrown fetch is resent, and the stream watchdog and recovery accounting are untouched. The 1948 comment change is correct.
- **Removing `replayable`.** The doc and the code both say a resend needs a URL under a configured endpoint. That is correct: bodies are all `JSON.stringify` strings, so the guard was dead.

### Suggestions
- `cli/src/client.ts:905` (Low). `if (key &amp;&amp; resends === 0) this.staleResends.delete(key)` clears the budget on any `Response`, including 5xx or 429, and also when the body dies after headers.
  - Trigger: a gateway that alternates a reset with a 502/503 gets a fresh budget every cycle.
  - Fix: clear only when `response.ok` is true or the status is below 500. This is optional, because the bound per cycle is the same 4 sends.
- `cli/src/client.ts:921` (note). The count semantic is "3rd charged failure stops", so effectively 3 extra sends per minute across requests, which matches the docs. Fine as written.
- `cli/test/provider_healthy_server.test.ts` concurrent test. It depends on sockets being fresh at resend time and on the server's kill-the-second-request rule. It looks deterministic, since resends open new connections before any response returns. If it flakes, increase N or assert on `race.killed` only. I could not run it.
- I did not verify that the concurrent and probe tests are red against `8541146a`. Reading the code, the probe test is red if the budget key ignored the method, and the concurrent test is red if the first failure is charged.

  - **Trigger:** `restoreConversation` calls `restoreSession`, which replaces `this.messages`, the objective, the findings and the task state in `agent.ts:2121-2144`. That replaces the record of the session the operator was in with the other session's conversation. Before this delta the id was set first, so conversation and id stayed paired and the worst case was a partial restore saved under its own id.

### Checks you asked for
- **Escape and bidi injection:** `flat` makes C0, DEL, C1, U+2028/9 and the embedding and isolate overrides visible. The Rust `review_lines` then runs every row through `approval_safe_text`, which covers LRM, RLM, ALM, zero-width and tag characters. The sweep adds two delete kinds with `bad` injected.
- **Forged rows:**

  - Content rows always carry the `▎ ` prefix, so a content line cannot pose as a statement row.

  - A truncated private-key block is withheld after its BEGIN line.

  - Backslashes treated as slashes.
  - An absolute path canonicalised, so a link is followed to its target.
  - A relative final link kept and judged for escaping the workspace, pointing into `.git`, or pointing at the root.
  - A directory refused without `recursive`.
  - A link to a directory with `recursive` removes only the link; `remove_dir_all` does not follow symlinks.
  - A dangling link ends in failure, as the engine does.
  - The only divergence is a lexical `.git` component reached through a `.git` symlink. The preview then says "Only this file is removed" while the engine refuses. That is the safe direction.

- **D-12 flag logic:**

  - It is consumed in `onToolEnd` only when `denied === true`.

<result>**No findings.**

**D-25 preview (`core/src/bin/nexus_tui/composer.rs`, `row_label` and its call in `layout`)**
- The new path puts the first line of a paste, which is untrusted clipboard text, into the composer row.
- `Composer::paste` keeps paste content raw (composer.rs:131-150). Only `insert` strips control characters (composer.rs:236). So the first line can contain ESC, OSC 52 or OSC 0 sequences.
- Those sequences cannot reach the terminal. The row is drawn through ratatui 0.30.2, which depends on ratatui-core 0.1.2. `Buffer::set_stringn` there drops any grapheme containing a control character (`ratatui-core-0.1.2/src/buffer/buffer.rs:351`). A leftover like `[31m` is shown as inert text.
- `row_label` only changes the row text. The sent prompt and the transcript still use `label()` (composer.rs:202, live_view.rs:491), so the paste content is not exposed to anyone new.
- The only residual is that bidi override characters, such as U+202E, are not control characters. They could make the user's own pasted line look reordered in the composer row. The user pasted it themselves and sees the same text elsewhere, so this is not an exploit path.
- `fit` and `row.width()` cap the row width, so there is no overflow or allocation concern. A paste of at most six lines is cheap to scan.

**`98d7804f` (`cli/src/startup_trust.ts` width fallback, `cli/test/helpers/tui_surface_driver.py` ctrl+r)**
- The width fallback only sanitizes a terminal-reported number. It is checked with `Number.isFinite`, `&gt; 0` and `Math.floor`, then used as a wrap width. This is a trust-prompt layout change, and the trust decision logic is untouched. Falling back to 80 cannot make the prompt skip or auto-accept trust.
- The `ctrl+r` edit is a test-only helper.

**`903ee3a4` (`core/src/bin/nexus_tui/live.rs`)**
- This is a test-only change to the viewport.

**Repository rules:** `REVIEW.md` and `CLAUDE.md` do not exist at `f327a410`. `AGENTS.md` has nothing that applies to this diff.

**Finding**

- **Severity:** low. **Confidence:** 0.55.
- **Location:** `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/composer.rs:46-52` (`Paste::row_label`), used at line 377 in `layout`.
- **Defect:** The first line of a paste goes into the composer row unfiltered. `paste()` keeps content exactly (only CR and CRLF become newlines), so the preview can contain control characters such as ESC or BEL. `insert()` strips these (lines 228-236) because they "would throw off the cursor column", and `row_label` does not. `layout` measures the row with `shown.width()`.
- **Trigger:** The user pastes 2 to 6 lines whose first non-blank line contains control characters, such as a copied ANSI-coloured log line (`\x1b[31merror…`).
- **Impact:** ratatui drops control graphemes when it draws the row (`render_composer`, `live_view.rs:1184`), so there is no escape injection. I did not confirm how `unicode-width` 0.2.3 counts a control character in a string. If it counts any width at all, the layout column and the cursor column no longer match what is drawn, and the preview shows leftovers such as `[31m`.
- **Fix:** Drop control characters in `row_label`, keeping the existing tab-to-space mapping:

```rust
let first: String = first.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control() || *c == '\t').collect();
format!("{label} {}…", first.replace('\t', " "))
```

**Checked and cleared**
- **D-25 behaviour:** The preview appears only in the layout row. `display` and `take` still use the label alone and the full content, as the Trail describes. Cursor movement and deletion treat the paste as one grapheme, so they are unaffected by the longer row text.
- **Width handling:** `fit` bounds the width. A blank-only paste falls back to the label. A trailing-newline paste of one line shows "1 line" with a preview, which is consistent.
- **`98d7804f` (`startup_trust.ts`):** The fallback correctly handles 0, undefined, NaN, Infinity and negative values. Columns of 1 or 2 give a non-positive wrap width, as they already did before.
- **`98d7804f` (`tui_surface_driver.py`):** The ctrl+r change matches the crash-screen hint at `live_view.rs:2035` for a non-empty draft.
- **`903ee3a4` (`live.rs` test):** `Terminal::with_options` with a `Fixed` viewport does not query the terminal size, and `Viewport` and `TerminalOptions` are exported at the ratatui root. This is test-only.
- **Version bump and docs:** No logic.</result>

# Nexus Code: evidence integrity audit and terminal-agent build specification

Audit date: November 12, 2026, Toronto time.

Audited source: `mikeholownych/nexus-code`, commit `f327a410d699c70c41b4280fba7ba3373d0bab2c` (merge of PR #482). Commit timestamp: 2026-11-13 01:52:29 UTC. Root and CLI packages declare 1.1.3; README describes 1.1.4 as development with qualification pending.

## 1. Scope and evidence limits

This is a targeted source audit of the execution, context, review and evaluation mechanisms relevant to the preceding Karpathy repository assessment. It is not a comprehensive security audit or release certification. The complete recursive GitHub tree was retrieved without truncation. Selected source, tests, CI and plans were fetched at the pinned commit. No production endpoint was contacted. No repository files were changed upstream.

Direct probes ran selected, unmodified, dependency-free TypeScript modules using Node v24.22.1's type stripping. They were not full installed-package tests. Full Rust/TypeScript builds, the complete suite, isolation checks and live inference were not run. Statements below distinguish reproduced function behavior from source-observed gaps and proposed additions. Source links are pinned to the audited commit.

## 2. Existing capabilities to retain

Do not reimplement these merely because the earlier architectural assessment suggested them:

| Capability | Existing implementation | Audit conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Independent review evidence packages and strict verdict parsing | `cli/src/core/independent_review.ts`; `operation_runner_execution.ts` | Implemented and used by review units. Implementer narrative is excluded; deterministic scope/failure checks exist. One acceptance gap is detailed below. |
| Verifier definition binding | `cli/src/core/independent_check.ts` | Substantial existing checks for changed tests, commands, dependencies and baseline evidence. Extend with adversarial tests rather than replacing. |
| Versioned evaluator and candidate isolation | `cli/src/eval_cli.ts`; `eval/runner_api.mjs`; `eval/run.mjs` | Existing installed-runtime invocation, candidate/evaluator separation, budgets and isolated hidden checks. Preserve this authority boundary. No new generic shell-based CERI executor. |
| Server request token counts and admission evidence | `cli/src/client.ts:1570`; `cli/src/agent.ts:3005-3205` | Already measures requests, distinguishes estimates, supports strict counting, and records counted/admitted worker differences. A recommendation to add counting from scratch would be wrong. |
| Durable session export | `cli/src/session_export.ts` | Carries task state, receipts, archived messages and explicit history completeness. Extend rather than create a second export format. |
| CERI foundation | `cli/src/ceri/` and `cli/test/ceri_*.test.ts` | Contracts, runner, store, comparator, reports, investigation and remediation abstractions exist. Their guarantees need strengthening before autonomous experimentation. |

Historical plans are context, not evidence of current runtime behavior. In particular, CERI's foundational end-to-end test supplies a mock boolean executor and an inline baseline containing `manifestSha256: "hash-001"`; it does not prove execution isolation or verified baseline provenance.

## 3. Findings

Severity refers to correctness of the affected evidence/review API. It does not establish exploitability across all release paths. The installed evaluator has separate controls; this audit does not establish that its scorer shares CERI's defects.

### F01. CERI can classify incomplete or empty evidence as PASS

**High; directly reproduced.** `CeriBaselineComparator.compareRuns` rejects several exceptional statuses but does not require a terminal executed status. It also permits an empty union of assertion IDs. With otherwise matching minimal inputs:

- `COMPLETED`, current `{}`, baseline `{}` produces `PASS`, confidence `1`.
- `RUNNING`, current `{x:true}`, baseline `{x:true}` produces `PASS`, confidence `1`.

The actual runner avoids executing zero assertions as a successful run, but the comparator is a public API that independently accepts these states. It lacks the expected assertion population needed to validate complete coverage.

Source: [baseline.ts](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/f327a410d699c70c41b4280fba7ba3373d0bab2c/cli/src/ceri/baseline.ts#L59), especially assertion comparison starting at L156.

### F02. Baseline identity and reproduction claims are not evidence-bound

**High; source observed with partial direct reproduction.** `checkComparability` compares evaluation ID/version, model name, quantization and current dirty status. It does not verify `manifestSha256`, model digest, sampling, routing, fixture/evaluator identity, or the declared `mandatoryComparabilityKeys`. A probe with a current model digest and an arbitrary baseline hash still produces `PASS`. The runner accepts caller-supplied baseline boolean maps, byREDACTEDing stored evidence.

Additionally, REDACTEDing `isRepeatReproduction=true` or `isPriorRegressionCandidate=true` is enough for `CONFIRMED_REGRESSION`; no second run identity or matching reproduced divergence is required by this API. The latter is source-observed, not a separately executed probe.

Different source commits are expected in a candidate comparison. The correction must compare non-treatment variables while explicitly identifying what changed, rather than requiring source commits to match.

Sources: [baseline.ts L12](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/f327a410d699c70c41b4280fba7ba3373d0bab2c/cli/src/ceri/baseline.ts#L12), [runner.ts L181](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/f327a410d699c70c41b4280fba7ba3373d0bab2c/cli/src/ceri/runner.ts#L181).

### F03. Coverage and report language can overstate execution

**High; directly reproduced.** Reporting adds every supplied evaluation ID to the executed set and uses `runs.length` as executed runs. One `NOT_EXECUTED` manifest with one available evaluation produces 100% `evidenceCompletenessScore`, one executed evaluation, zero REDACTEDes. A `RUNNING` manifest reaches the text: “NO REGRESSIONS OBSERVED: All executed evaluations (0) completed cleanly and match or exceed baseline criteria.” Completed runs without baseline comparisons can also reach that branch by inspection.

Coverage is also labelled evidence completeness without checking receipts or integrity.

Source: [reporting.ts L28](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/f327a410d699c70c41b4280fba7ba3373d0bab2c/cli/src/ceri/reporting.ts#L28), L51 and L127.

### F04. Unproven review criteria do not prevent ACCEPT

**High; parser reproduced, downstream completion source traced.** A valid JSON verdict with `verdict:"ACCEPT"`, no suspected defects or scope violations, and `unprovenCriteria:["Required crash recovery has not been demonstrated"]` remains `ACCEPT`. A REDACTEDing verifier does not necessarily cover that criterion. `operation_runner_execution.ts` checks only `verdict.verdict` and returns completed for this result; its successful summary drops the unproven list.

This is a concrete review-boundary gap, not a claim that every accepted review produces verified task completion.

Sources: [independent_review.ts L335](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/f327a410d699c70c41b4280fba7ba3373d0bab2c/cli/src/core/independent_review.ts#L335), [operation_runner_execution.ts L891](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/f327a410d699c70c41b4280fba7ba3373d0bab2c/cli/src/core/operation_runner_execution.ts#L891).

### F05. Evaluation definitions accept invalid contracts; runner budgets are declarative here

**Medium-high; validator reproduced, execution observations from source.** A definition with an invalid domain, negative steps, NaN timeout, duplicate assertion IDs and missing fixture/output fields REDACTEDes `validateEvaluationDefinition`. Assertion records are reduced into a map keyed by ID, so duplicate IDs can overwrite results. Assertion items themselves are not validated.

The CERI runner calls a caller-provided boolean executor. It does not enforce the declared timeout, steps, tokens, authorized tools or fixture isolation; it catches executor exceptions as assertion failure. Existing evaluator controls elsewhere are stronger. The safe fix is integration with them and structured execution receipts, not executing `assertion.command` directly.

Sources: [contracts.ts L208](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/f327a410d699c70c41b4280fba7ba3373d0bab2c/cli/src/ceri/contracts.ts#L208), [runner.ts L126](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/f327a410d699c70c41b4280fba7ba3373d0bab2c/cli/src/ceri/runner.ts#L126).

### F06. CERI integrity records are written, but evidence loading does not verify them

**High for authoritative CERI use; source observed.** `finalizeRun` hashes files and writes a local integrity record. `loadAssertions` reads and trusts assertion contents without checking that record; array records use `Boolean(item.REDACTEDed)`, so a stored string `"false"` becomes true. Object maps are cast without runtime validation. `initRun` uses recursive directory creation and replaces a manifest rather than rejecting a reused run identity. Timestamp-only run IDs also risk collisions. Path checks are lexical and do not independently reject symlinked ancestors. Atomic rename is present, but explicit file/directory sync is absent from this store.

A local hash inventory is not tamper-proof. A writer able to replace both evidence and its inventory can recompute hashes. Authenticity requires a trusted expected root or stronger external authority. Do not promise immutable evidence from same-user filesystem writes.

Source: [evidence_store.ts L116](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/f327a410d699c70c41b4280fba7ba3373d0bab2c/cli/src/ceri/evidence_store.ts#L116), L171, L222 and L299.

### F07. Empirical efficiency comparisons accept different task populations

**Medium; directly reproduced.** `ComparativeEvaluationHarness.evaluateTraces` aggregates by configuration without pairing scenario/run populations or requiring task success. Config A running scenario `a` with 1,000 tokens and config B running unrelated scenario `different` with 10 tokens produces 99% efficiency improvement. This arithmetic is correct but the comparison is not meaningful.

`runBenchmark` is already documented as assumption-driven projection. Retain that disclosure; do not call the synthetic multipliers empirical evidence.

Source: [comparative_harness.ts L64](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/blob/f327a410d699c70c41b4280fba7ba3373d0bab2c/cli/src/eval/comparative_harness.ts#L64).

### Extensions requiring repository-wide confirmation before implementation

The reviewed request receipt records model, endpoint, usage and outcome, but does not contain a canonical context manifest identifying all selected/excluded source material. Session export is richer but is not a record of each final sanitized request. Treat a request-bound manifest as a proposed extension pending a complete call-site search.

No bounded campaign implementation was identified in the inspected paths/tree names. Absence from this sample is not proof of repository-wide absence. Search current HEAD before introducing it. Likewise, a string comparison between remediation author/reviewer labels is not authenticated principal separation; do not elevate that utility into a security claim.

## 4. Terminal-agent build specification

The remainder is the execution instruction. Follow it against the current checkout, reconciling changes since the audited commit. Complete implementation and validation in reviewable slices. Do not stop after producing another plan.

### Mission

Strengthen Nexus's existing evidence/review mechanisms, then implement controlled experiments and inspectable request provenance. Adopt the useful principles from Karpathy's autoresearch, micrograd and rendergit without importing their permissive execution assumptions. Accuracy and defensible outcomes outrank latency or token savings.

### Phase 0: establish and protect the baseline

1. Read root and applicable nested AGENTS.md, current release plan, `docs/v1.0.0/CONCURRENCY.md`, `docs/v1.1.2/CERI_PLAN.md`, and current development/test guidance. The audited root instructions require an isolated worktree/branch, atomic slice/hot-file claims when work may overlap, isolated test HOME, a GATEWAY claim for inference, and owner-controlled push/tag/publish. Do not modify the canonical checkout or unrelated work.
2. Record HEAD, branch, status, build identity, toolchain versions, supported test commands and environment limitations. Recheck each finding against current code. Classify already fixed findings explicitly; do not resurrect old behavior.
3. Use XERJ for nontrivial analogue research as instructed by AGENTS.md. If unavailable, record the reason and inspect public peer source. Never query corpora for held-out evaluation tasks. Preserve licence provenance for borrowed ideas/code.
4. Run baseline targeted tests in an isolated environment. Add failing regressions for F01-F07 before changing their implementation. Record existing unrelated failures separately.
5. Create `docs/engineering/evidence-integrity/PLAN.md`, `FINDINGS.md` and an evidence index, or adapt an existing canonical location. Do not silently change release version or claim 1.1.4 qualification.

### Slice A: correct review acceptance and report truthfulness

Modify `independent_review.ts`, relevant operation integration/tests, and CERI reporting/contracts.

- An ACCEPT with unresolved required criteria must become REJECT or an explicit inconclusive result that cannot complete the review unit. Initially treat every existing `unprovenCriteria` entry as required. If optional advisories are needed, introduce a distinct typed field and requirement IDs rather than letting prose waive requirements.
- Preserve the complete structured verdict, evidence references and rejection reasons in durable operation records; do not replace them with a short success narrative.
- Separate scheduled, started, evaluated and successfully completed counts. NOT_EXECUTED and RUNNING never count as executed evaluation coverage. A cancelled/interrupted run may have consumed resources without completing an evaluation: report both facts separately.
- Compute evaluation coverage from the known evaluation population and verified terminal evidence. Distinguish it from evidence completeness. Unknown evaluation IDs, duplicate run IDs and counts exceeding the denominator must be rejected or explicitly diagnosed.
- Never print baseline-equivalence claims without eligible verified comparisons. RUNNING, absent comparisons, absent evidence or zero completed evaluations must produce an explicit pending/insufficient-evidence result.

Acceptance: reproduce F03/F04 as failing tests first; both parser and operation-runner integration must reject unresolved criteria. Table-test every RunStatus and missing/invalid comparison. No optimistic fallback branch may classify unknown state as success.

### Slice B: contracts and evidence lifecycle

Extend existing CERI types with versioned runtime validation; use existing repository validation/durable-write utilities where suitable.

- Validate enums; nonempty normalized IDs; finite positive integer budgets; fixture/output/tool/criteria element types; assertion schema, unique IDs and nonempty descriptions; regex syntax where applicable; numeric sampling ranges. Reject unsupported fields/versions where ambiguity affects authority. An explicitly empty evaluation remains non-certifying and inconclusive, never PASS.
- Replace bare assertion booleans for authoritative runs with typed execution receipts. Include assertion ID, command/validator identity, expected and observed results, exit/signal, start/end, timeout/cancellation/resource/output-limit state, artifact references and hashes, execution identity and evidence authority.
- Failures of assertions, infrastructure, evaluation machinery and operator cancellation remain distinct. Exceptions must not silently become product regressions.
- Generate collision-resistant run IDs. Reserve run directories exclusively. Refuse reuse, duplicate finalization and writes after finalization. Use one run handle per active run; do not allow a second initialization to redirect the first run's events.
- Strictly validate stored booleans/receipts. Reject strings, unknown IDs, duplicate assertions and incomplete expected assertion sets.
- Verify artifact inventory and expected integrity root before accepting baseline/current records. Detect changed, missing and unexpected files, symlinks and non-regular files. Do not follow symlinked evidence paths outside the configured root. Use private permissions and existing safe filesystem mechanisms; state residual same-user/TOCTOU limits honestly.
- Use crash-consistent persistence with bounded records and recoverable interrupted state. Reuse `core/durable_file.ts` and related guards after checking their guarantees. Quarantine partial/corrupt records rather than converting them into REDACTEDing evidence.
- Compare only persisted final manifests. Avoid returning a separately mutated manifest whose timestamps differ from what the store actually hashed.
- Bind comparison records into the finalized evidence bundle, or create a separately finalized derived record that explicitly names the immutable input roots. The current runner compares after finalization; do not silently append unbound results.

Acceptance: tests cover malformed disk records including `REDACTEDed:"false"`, directory/run collisions, symlink escape, concurrent run handles, evidence mutation, missing/extra files, interrupted write/restart, and post-finalization writes. Recomputed local hashes alone must never be described as authenticated external confirmation.

### Slice C: baseline eligibility and paired comparisons

- Introduce a verified baseline loader; authoritative comparisons cannot accept inline boolean maps or unchecked `manifestSha256` values. Keep synthetic/unit-test inputs through an explicitly non-certifying adapter if needed.
- Bind evaluation definition and expected assertions, fixture/dataset, evaluator build, candidate build/source/diff, model identity/quantization, sampling, task distribution, routing/profile configuration, toolchain/environment constraints and execution budgets.
- Define campaign treatment variables separately from comparability keys. A routing experiment may vary routing; a harness patch may vary source. Record those allowed differences explicitly. Unknown mandatory identity produces INCOMPARABLE, not equality by missing fields. Hardware must be controlled or stratified for performance claims.
- Require terminal executed evidence and nonempty complete assertion sets. Explicitly reject RUNNING, unknown states, empty sets, unverified hashes and incomplete baselines.
- Replace caller booleans for confirmed regression with distinct verified reproduction run references. Require equivalent non-treatment variables and the same failing requirement/assertion; a duplicate run ID is not reproduction. Preserve raw run outcomes even when a campaign is flaky.
- Pair empirical traces by task/version/run/seed or a declared matched population. Require comparable success status and budgets. Missing cells, unequal populations and unknown usage yield INCOMPARABLE or incomplete metrics, not percentage savings.
- Separate measured runs from synthetic projections in result types and reports. Use sample counts and observed variance; remove ungrounded confidence=1.0 interpretations. Never interpret a deterministic classification flag as statistical certainty.

Acceptance: F01/F02/F07 regressions; mismatched model digest, fixture, evaluator, sampling, profile and budget; allowed treatment differences; baseline hash mismatch; empty/partial/missing runs; fake reproduction and distinct valid reproduction; cheap failed runs cannot beat expensive successful ones.

### Slice D: connect CERI to the existing trusted evaluator

Inspect `eval_cli.ts`, `eval/runner_api.mjs`, `eval/run.mjs`, `eval/score.mjs`, dataset and isolation modules before designing the adapter.

- Keep the evaluator external to the candidate's writable/runtime closure. The candidate cannot edit hidden fixtures, authoritative scoring or evaluator output.
- Adapt existing versioned-evaluation artifacts into validated CERI manifests/receipts. Preserve original hashes, dataset split, installed build identity, containment findings, tool receipts and precise failure taxonomy.
- Enforce timeout/steps/tokens/tools through existing runtime boundaries. Where a budget cannot be enforced, label it unsupported and refuse qualification requiring it.
- Pass cancellation to the actual executor and terminate the owned process/cgroup tree. Promise.race without terminating execution is insufficient. No automatic cloud fallback or alternate disclosure destination for an evaluator failure.
- A dry-run/mock executor must stay labelled synthetic; it cannot establish a baseline or certify an improvement.
- Retain existing CLI behavior and packaged-runtime compatibility. Provide a small read-only CERI import/inspect/compare interface using the established command structure; do not invent a parallel evaluator command system.

Acceptance: an installed-package vertical slice executes a development fixture, produces independently verified artifacts, imports them, compares against a verified baseline, and renders truthful reports. Exercise timeout, cancellation, containment failure and evaluator corruption. Prove evaluator/hidden artifacts remain inaccessible to the candidate. Never use held-out task contents to tune the implementation.

### Slice E: inspectable request-context manifests

First search all request, tracing, session and instruction-loading paths to avoid duplication. Extend the existing receipt/export system.

- Construct a context manifest at the final outbound serialization boundary after egress quarantine/sanitization, for each actual execution attempt and protocol. Record request/attempt/session/turn/step IDs, endpoint/model identity, selected tool-schema hash, instruction versions/provenance, repository state, source/range references and hashes, omissions/truncation reasons, compaction lineage and count source/reserves/limits version.
- Bind the manifest to the exact sanitized request body using a defined digest over exact serialized bytes or a documented canonical representation. Never hash one representation and send a separately rebuilt mutable body. Retries and failovers need distinct attempt records; record counted/admitted worker differences using existing mechanisms.
- Do not duplicate raw prompts or secrets by default. Redacted export content must identify its transformation; do not claim its hash equals the original private payload. Evaluate keyed digests or retention controls for low-entropy sensitive inputs. No keys/credentials in manifests.
- Initially record provenance only where known. A manifest must distinguish complete, partial and unknown provenance; do not invent file lineage for arbitrary conversation strings.
- Add a human-readable context view and JSON export through existing session/receipt surfaces. Show what was included, excluded, compacted and unavailable. Preserve complete references when the UI truncates display.
- Preserve existing exact-token counting, strict admission, fallback uncertainty and provider-disclosure behavior. Do not replace these with minbpe or a new generic tokenizer.

Acceptance: identical final request has a reproducible digest; relevant body changes alter it; secret redaction does not leak input; protocol conversion and retries are correctly bound; compaction links old/new manifests; same alias resolving to a different worker/model is visible. Malicious source delimiters cannot become trusted instructions through rendering/serialization.

### Slice F: independent reference checks for recovery

Add a small test-only reference reducer/checker that does not import the production state transition or completion logic it is checking. Use explicit scenario tables and property/metamorphic checks rather than a second full orchestrator.

- Given durable events, reconstruct expected requirements, steering application, operation state, attempt receipts and unresolved side-effect status.
- Compare with production restoration under duplicated, reordered, missing and truncated events; termination before/after an external side effect; compaction and restart; stale verification receipts; unknown execution status.
- Never promise exactly-once external side effects merely because a request ID exists. Require tool idempotency guarantees or record unresolved outcome and reconcile before retry.
- Assert that unknown execution cannot become success, cancelled work cannot become verified, missing provenance cannot become trusted, and compaction preserves unresolved requirements/evidence references.

Acceptance: mutation tests or deliberately faulty fixtures demonstrate that the checker detects at least one restoration defect independently of production logic. Generated randomized cases use recorded seeds and bounded execution.

### Slice G: bounded experimentation, after A-D REDACTED

Implement only once authoritative result handling is corrected. Reuse CERI and the installed evaluator.

Campaign specification must include ID/version, hypothesis, baseline root, candidate source/config, allowed treatment variables and edit scope, development task population, protected holdout policy, repetitions, per-run and total time/step/token/cost limits, maximum candidates, concurrency, cancellation/stall rules, and promotion criteria.

- Start with explicit candidate commits/configurations. An agent-generated candidate is optional and must use an isolated worktree, preserve rejected patches, obey the allowed scope and leave evaluator/authority code protected.
- Persist every candidate/run transition and permit resume without reclassifying unknown in-flight execution as complete. Enforce campaign budgets across restart, retries and child requests, not once per process.
- Preserve failed, rejected and crashed experiments with their reasons. Never reset the operator checkout or erase negative evidence.
- Correctness is lexically prior to efficiency: any required correctness regression vetoes promotion. Performance comparisons require matched successful populations and sufficiently supported usage/timing measurements.
- Promotion produces a reviewable proposal and verified evidence bundle. It does not merge, deploy, change production routing, publish a release or approve its own work. Existing authority rules remain in force.
- Use development fixtures for iteration. A genuinely reserved holdout must remain inaccessible until qualification; repeated evaluation on publicly visible fixtures is regression testing, not evidence of unseen generalization.
- Default to the configured local gateway. Take the required GATEWAY claim before inference. Keep live campaigns small and explicitly resource-bounded; do not contend with active operator work.

Acceptance: a deterministic development campaign with one correct improvement, one cheaper incorrect candidate, one cancelled run and one infrastructure failure records all results correctly; only the correct candidate becomes proposal-eligible. Restart preserves consumed budgets. Exhaustion/stall/cancel stops owned work. No merge or production configuration changes occur.

## 5. Validation and delivery requirements

1. For each slice: record the failing regression, implement the smallest compatible fix, run targeted tests, and inspect the diff. Use repository test runner conventions rather than assuming raw Node TypeScript execution matches supported Node 22.
2. Run TypeScript build and relevant CLI/evaluator/operation tests. Before final handoff run the repository's required aggregate checks, including Rust and security/terminal checks where applicable. Use documented CI fixtures for evaluator tests; do not mislabel missing bubblewrap/cgroups/tmpfs as a product failure or a REDACTEDing check. `make test-ci` provisions fixtures according to current docs. Do not casually run privileged host changes.
3. Verify installed-package behavior for evaluator integration and new CLI/export surfaces, not only source-module tests. Preserve Node 22/24 compatibility and generated-file policy in CI.
4. Perform a separate skeptical final review against this specification, original task and evidence. If another agent is used under applicable repository instructions, give it the original requirements and evidence, without implementer conclusions. Otherwise document an independent review procedure and its limits; do not label self-review external confirmation.
5. Deliver an updated findings ledger, design decisions, changed paths, test commands/results, evidence/artifact hashes, compatibility/migration notes, limitations and remaining blockers. Link reproduction and qualification evidence to exact source/build identities. No invented percentages or readiness claims.
6. Leave push, merge, tags, publishing and production routing changes to the owner. This task authorizes implementation in reviewable local slices, not production promotion.

Definition of done: F01-F07 are fixed or explicitly shown already fixed at current HEAD; protected evaluator integration REDACTEDes; request context provenance and recovery checks work with stated limits; bounded campaigns cannot promote unverified/incorrect candidates; all required checks REDACTED or material environment blockers are precisely documented. A plan, mocked vertical slice, green self-authored assertions, or model agreement alone does not satisfy completion.

- Severity: medium (low if you rate by how often it is hit; the module is unwired)
